maple-api.statement: MMIO queue operations initialize and bind queues, enqueue data or pointers, and consume values. PRODUCE_PTR requests a fetch whose value is delivered through a queue; LIMA_PRODUCE supplies an indexed range of values to a queue, while LIMA and PREFETCH target the LLC.
limitations: API names and abstract arguments are described, but concrete C types, header, packing and index-width domains are not established by this paper.

maple-lima.statement: LIMA accepts two array bases and caller-provided begin/end bounds for A[B[i]]; A=0 requests B[i]. It reads adjacent B data in 64-byte chunks into scratchpad, computes target addresses word by word, and feeds pointer-fetch or LLC-prefetch requests into the produce path.
limitations: Caller-provided range bounds do not prove autonomous nested CSR traversal or arbitrary index functions.
A shared B chunk is not evidence that arbitrary A addresses are sorted or merged by locality.

maple-queue-order.locator: PDF pp.5–6, §3.1 produce/consume timeline and §3.4, Figs.3,6
maple-queue-order.statement: A pointer fetch reserves a FIFO slot and uses its slot index as the memory transaction ID. Out-of-order memory replies are deposited into the associated reserved slots, preserving the software-visible queue sequence. Consumes take values from the queue head.
limitations: Per-queue value association does not establish global order across queues, cores or memory updates.

maple-acknowledgement.locator: PDF p.5, §3.1 steps 1–6 and A–C; p.7 §3.6
maple-acknowledgement.statement: The core retires the pointer-produce store on MAPLE acknowledgement before the memory reply arrives. The reply later fills the reserved queue entry. A consume finishes when its load response returns the queue value.
limitations: Pointer-produce acknowledgement is not fetched-data readiness or a general shared-memory visibility fence.

maple-stable-data.statement: Requests can select coherent LLC loads or noncoherent direct-memory loads. Queue scratchpad values have no coherence guarantee after fetch; the compiler or DSL must ensure fetched arrays receive no further writes during their use, with epoch-separated updates discussed as an example.
limitations: Coherent fetch routing does not make a previously queued value track later CPU writes.
Concurrent parent CAS in the current BFS source does not satisfy this stable-array condition merely because the proposed engine operation is a read.

maple-future-atomics.statement: Read-modify-write atomics are mentioned as a possible extension of the programming model. The examined API and implementation description establishes loads, queues and prefetching, not a MAPLE CAS executor.
limitations: An extensible opcode space is not current CAS support; absence of a contract is recorded as unknown, not a universal impossibility.

tmu-fig8.locator: PDF p6, Fig. 8 lines 2–21; §4.4; PDF p5 §4.2
tmu-fig8.statement: Fig8 traverses row pointers with DnsFbrT(0,num_rows), broadcasts row begin/end to two RngFbrT lanes with offsets 0/1 and stride 2, loads column indexes and nnz values, loads b through column indexes, LockStep-marshals paired vectors, and registers GITE ri and GEND re.
limitations: Two lanes are the illustration, not the Table 5 evaluated eight-lane system or a legal tuning interval. Boundaries require padding or an msk predicate (§4.2); Fig8 omits a concrete predicate/padding ABI.

tmu-cpu.locator: PDF p5 Fig. 4; PDF p6 Fig. 6 and §4.3
tmu-cpu.statement: TMU supplies required operands and ordered callback IDs. CPU ri multiplies vector operands and reduces/accumulates into sum; CPU re stores x[i++] and resets sum.
limitations: A CPU store is not a TMU scatter capability; CPU reduction is not TMU arithmetic.

tmu-outq.statement: Head/body/tail callbacks have IDs and scalar/vector/predicate operands. TG output FSMs serialize across groups with previous/next waiting states to preserve callback/operand order. outQ and its buffers are double-buffered; the core processes a full chunk while TMU fills another.
limitations: Callback order is not physical memory-response order or global CPU visibility. Ready/consumed acknowledgment, reuse and final partial chunk protocol are unspecified in inspected sections.

tmu-unknowns.statement: Inspected primary sections do not establish concrete configuration/register encodings, numeric widths, physical response tags, chunk ownership/consumption/finalpartial protocol or complete fault/drain/replay ordering.
limitations: Evidence limit only; unknown is not unsupported.

cobra-init.statement: bininit operands are cache-level identifier, number of reserved ways, number of unique indices, and tuple size in bytes. It reserves ways, computes the smallest power-of-two bin range whose C-Buffers fit, stores the range, and records actually used ways so unused reserved capacity can be reclaimed.
limitations: No encoding, header, C prototype, error convention or complete legal configuration interval is specified.

cobra-insert.statement: binupdate takes an index and update value and appends that pair to the selected L1 C-Buffer. Index high bits select buffer/set/way after removing log2(bin range) low bits. Per-buffer counters select the next tuple slot and wrap when full. C-Buffers are not byte addressable and exist outside shared-memory address space.
limitations: The supplied index selects a partition, not a direct store to the application destination address. No old destination value is returned by this collection contract.

cobra-hierarchy.statement: Hardware-managed per-level cacheline C-Buffers collect tuples over progressively narrower index ranges; full L1/L2 buffers are unpacked and repartitioned into next-level C-Buffers; full LLC buffers go to per-thread memory bins. This combines inexpensive small-buffer-set Binning with many bins for Accumulate.
limitations: Coalescing here means tuple collection, not same-index arithmetic reduction.

cobra-memory-bins.statement: Each thread has contiguous tuples per bin with precomputed counts and starting BinOffset entries. An unnamed ISA instruction initializes LLC tag offsets from buffer ID and starting offset. A full LLC buffer writes to BinBasePtr + BinOffset[binID], advances the offset by its tuple count, and resets its counter.
limitations: The text alternates pointer/offset and tuple-count descriptions; physical byte scaling and register binding are not a specified ABI. Bin base initialization and the unnamed instruction’s encoding remain unknown.

cobra-flush.locator: PDF p. 8, §V.E, Flushing the Cache After Binning
cobra-flush.statement: binflush marks end of Binning. Each core walks nonempty C-Buffers serially, L1 then L2 then its LLC bank, writing residual tuples to memory; eviction buffers, binning engines and offset logic must handle partial lines using tuple counters. All remaining tuples must reach bins before Accumulate.
limitations: Paper states the phase requirement, but does not specify a software-visible done/ack event, inter-core join, memory ordering/fence semantics, cancellation, or global write completion. binupdate retirement alone cannot release Accumulate.

cobra-phase-boundary.statement: PB materializes index/value tuples during Binning, then software Accumulate reads bins and applies destination updates. Neighbor-Populate bins (e.src,e.dst); Algorithm 2 partitions bins across Accumulate workers and uses ordinary Add on offsets, whereas Algorithm 1 uses AtomicAdd. Unordered neighbor lists permit the changed order.
limitations: No general permission to reorder noncommutative operations or floating-point arithmetic; no hardware destination update/atomic executor.
